body:
Fixes #2189.

Follow-through PR for #2189. The first half shipped in [#2191](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2191) / `2.16.0` with **one requirement still open**: R2 asked for a killed session to be continued *in the same `$` session / container*, and `$` could not do that yet. This repository filed three upstream issues from that case study — [`link-foundation/start#162`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/162) (`--resume`), [`#164`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/164) (argv flattened with `join(' ')`), [`#165`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/165) (a V8 self-abort reported as `oomKilled=false`) — and **all three are delivered in `start-command@0.33.0`**.

The scope comment asked for the rest too:

> We need to finish this issue by actually updating https://github.com/link-foundation/start (as we reported issues there and they are now delivered) and all other dependencies we have in the repository. We also should see what changed, and use all relevant best practices from all our dependencies in all our supported languages.

So this PR closes R2, consumes what 0.33.0 delivers, and moves every other dependency forward — with the three that were *behaviour* changes handled rather than only bumped.

## 1. Same-container resume — requirement R2 (`78a6a679`)

`src/isolation-runner.resume.lib.mjs` wraps `$ --resume <id> [-- <command>]`, and `src/session-kill-resume.in-place.lib.mjs` makes it the **preferred** recovery path: the clone, the caches and the half-finished branch survive the kill instead of being rebuilt from scratch. When in-place resume is unavailable or refused, the previous behaviour — a fresh isolated run — still happens, and *why* is recorded on the session record (`killRecoveryInPlace`, `killRecoveryResumeMode`) and in the operator's report, so "resumed" and "restarted" are never conflated.

## 2. No more limbo executions (`df9dc818`)

The bot reconciles at startup with `$ --resume-all`: a container still running is re-attached to, and one that ended while unsupervised is finalized **with the exit code it actually had** — the state the incident report described as a session nobody could account for.

## 3. `$` refusals are read as refusals (`1211d554`)

`command-stream`'s `` $ `` **resolves** on a non-zero exit instead of throwing. Every `$` invocation therefore looked successful, including `$ --stop <unknown>`:

```
$ --stop u-9
Error: No execution found with UUID or session name: u-9     (stderr, exit 1)
→ reported to the operator as: stopped
```

Every call site now inspects the exit code. The resume wrappers additionally separate **an older `$` that does not know the verb** (`unsupported: true`, so callers keep their previous path) from **a genuine refusal** (`"Session … is still running"`), which are the same exit code and must not be treated the same way.

## 4. 0.33.0's kill hints are consumed (`60750f4a`)

`exitReason` and `memoryExhausted` from `$ --status` feed `describeKillCause` directly, so a runtime self-abort is named as out of memory from the supervisor's own answer — not only from log forensics as in #2191.

## 5. Every dependency updated, and what changed in them used

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `start-command` (both images) | 0.32.1 | **0.33.0** |
| `@changesets/cli` | 2.31.0 | **3.0.1** |
| `jscpd` | 4.0.5 | **5.1.2** |
| `@sentry/node`, `@sentry/profiling-node` | 10.62.0 | **10.73.0** |
| `prettier` | 3.8.5 | **3.9.6** |
| `agent-commander` | 0.8.0 | **0.10.1** |
| `dayjs` | 1.11.21 | **1.11.23** |
| `eslint` | 10.5.0 | **10.9.1** |
| `lint-staged` | 17.0.8 | **17.4.1** |
| `secretlint` (3 packages) | 13.0.2 | **13.0.5** |
| `lino-objects-codec` | 0.4.0 | **0.8.0** |
| `lino-i18n` | 0.1.1 | **0.2.0** |

Three of those were not just version numbers.

### `@changesets/cli` 2 → 3 breaks the release job

`changeset version` now **exits 1** when there are no unreleased changesets; 2.x warned and exited 0. From the installed 3.0.1 dist:

```js
if (changesets.length === 0) {
  logger.warn('No unreleased changesets found, exiting.');
  throw new ExitError(1);
}
```

The release workflow reads the changeset count *before* rebasing onto the remote, and the rebase can consume the very changesets the release decision was made on (a concurrent run versioned them first). Under 2.x that was a no-op; under 3.x it is a red release job for a repository in a perfectly fine state. `versionAndCommit` re-reads the count after the rebase and reports the already-published version through the existing `already_released` contract. Reproduced first, then fixed: `tests/test-issue-2189-changesets-3-version-guard.mjs`.

### `jscpd` 4 → 5 silently loosened the duplication gate

jscpd 5 is a Rust rewrite, and `skipComments` is an **unknown field** in it — it warns and falls back to `mode: mild`. `--debug` prints the merged config (`experiments/issue-2189/jscpd5-config-keys.sh`):

```
with "skipComments": true   →  Warning: unknown field `skipComments` …   "mode": "mild"
with "mode": "weak"         →  "mode": "weak"
```

`.jscpd.json` now says `"mode": "weak"`, which is what the old option means in 5.

### `@sentry/node` 10.71+ turns structured logs on by default — and they bypass `beforeSend`

`enableLogs` now defaults to `true`, and structured logs go through `beforeSendLog`; `beforeSend` never sees them. The redaction this repository relies on was therefore no longer covering everything that left the process. `src/instrument.sanitize.lib.mjs` is now shared between `beforeSend` and a new `beforeSendLog` hook, so both surfaces are scrubbed by the same code (`tests/test-issue-2189-sentry-log-sanitization.mjs`).

`node-pty` (new, via `agent-commander` 0.10's real-TUI capture) is denied a native build in `allowScripts`: it runs in a **separate spawned pty host** that this repository never launches headlessly, and the import path used here works without it.

Two more were checked and deliberately recorded as **not** affecting this repository, rather than claimed: dayjs 1.11.22's DST-offset fix is not reproducible with any call shape in this codebase (`experiments/issue-2189/dayjs-tz-dst.mjs` — identical offsets on both versions), while 1.11.23's `RangeError: Invalid time value` fix **is** (`experiments/issue-2189/dayjs-tz-invalid.mjs`).

## Case study

Everything above is written up with its evidence in **[`docs/case-studies/issue-2189/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2189-b28225043d62/docs/case-studies/issue-2189/README.md)** under **Dependency Follow-Through**, including the version table, the quoted upstream sources for each claim, and the one improvement deliberately deferred (jscpd 5's `--baseline-from-ref` / `--fail-on-new-clones`, which needs a baseline commit this PR should not pick).

## Tests

New:

- `tests/test-issue-2189-start-command-0.33.mjs` — the 0.33.0 status hints
- `tests/test-issue-2189-isolation-resume.mjs` — both resume wrappers end to end against a stub `$`, including the non-zero-exit and unsupported-verb paths
- `tests/test-issue-2189-same-container-resume.mjs` — R2, including every case in-place resume must refuse
- `tests/test-issue-2189-startup-resume-all.mjs` — startup reconciliation
- `tests/test-issue-2189-changesets-3-version-guard.mjs` — the changesets 3.0 release race
- `tests/test-issue-2189-sentry-log-sanitization.mjs` — `beforeSendLog` redaction

Two existing tests needed attention, for different reasons:

- `tests/test-issue-1980-docker-cleanup.mjs` asserts on the *source text* of the module holding `findStartCommandBinary`. That function moved to `src/start-command-cli.lib.mjs` — the resume wrappers need the `$` loader without importing the runner and creating a cycle — so the assertion was retargeted at the module that now holds the guarantee; the guarantee itself is unchanged.
- `tests/test-issue-2135-log-explosion.mjs` caught this PR's *own* new code. Its "every spawner reports the signal rather than interpolating a null code" guard forbids `exited with code ${code}` in spawner sources, and the first draft of the `$` wrappers wrote exactly that in `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs` and `src/isolation-runner.resume.lib.mjs`. Both now report through `describeChildExit`, and `src/isolation-runner.resume.lib.mjs` was added to the guard's file list so the module this PR introduced is held to the same rule.

commits.messageBody:
…164, #165)

`$ --status` and `$ --list` now carry three additive fields on a finished
execution: `exitReason` (e.g. `memory-exhaustion (v8-heap-limit)`),
`memoryExhausted` and `memoryExhaustedReason` (the log line carrying the
evidence). Upstream derives them from the same log tail it already reads for
the exit footer, and only for an abnormal exit.

Parse them from JSON, links-notation and text output, and feed them into
`describeKillCause`. This catches the case the local scan structurally cannot:
the fatal line scrolled out of the bounded window Hive Mind re-reads, but `$`
saw it when the command exited.

They stay hints, never verdicts:
  - a clean exit (code 0) is never upgraded;
  - a non-memory `exitReason` is reported as evidence but does not change the
    cause;
  - memory mechanisms are matched by the `memory-exhaustion` prefix, so a new
    upstream mechanism classifies correctly without a Hive Mind release;
  - absent fields parse as null (unknown), never false;
  - the local log-marker scan is unchanged and still reaches the verdict on its
    own, so behaviour does not regress on an older `$` binary.

Refs #2189

…d 0.33.0)

start-command 0.33.0 delivers link-foundation/start#162, the capability
issue #2189 was missing: re-entering an existing execution instead of
starting a fresh isolated run, and reconciling executions whose watcher
died with the process that launched them.

Adds src/start-command-cli.lib.mjs (the `$` loader and PATH lookup, moved
out of the runner so the new wrappers can use them without an import
cycle) and src/isolation-runner.resume.lib.mjs. Both verbs degrade
gracefully: an older `$` build reports `unsupported` rather than throwing,
so callers keep their previous behaviour.

command-stream's `$` resolves on a non-zero exit instead of throwing, so
the new resume wrappers — and the pre-existing `stopIsolatedSession` —
read every refusal as a success. Found by running the wrappers against a
real `$`: 0.32.1 answers `--resume-all` with
`Error: Unknown wrapper option: --resume-all` on stderr and exit 1, and
the wrapper reported `success: true` with an empty parse. `$ --stop` on an
unknown UUID behaves the same way, which made a session nobody stopped
look handled.

Both now inspect the exit code, and the unsupported-verb probe matches
0.32.1's actual wording ("Unknown *wrapper* option").

experiments/issue-2189-start-command-resume.mjs runs both wrappers against
whichever `$` is on PATH; verified green on 0.33.0 (docker-snapshot fields
parsed, --resume-all reconciled three executions) and degrading cleanly on
0.32.1. tests/test-issue-2189-isolation-resume.mjs covers the same ground
hermetically with a stub `$` (35 assertions).
commits.messageHeadline: fix(isolation): read `$` exit codes; verify resume wrappers end to end

commits.messageBody:
start-command@0.33.0 delivers `$ --resume <id> -- <command>` (filed from this
issue as link-foundation/start#162), which commits the stopped container's
filesystem and runs the recovery command in a container derived from it. The
killed session's clone, caches and half-finished branch survive, and the
execution UUID is preserved so `--status`/`--list`/`--upload-log` keep
addressing one logical session.

- src/session-kill-resume.in-place.lib.mjs: the policy and the attempt. Formal
  AI (#2146) and `--use-router` tasks are deliberately excluded — their
  internal Docker networks are attached with `docker network connect` after
  the container is created, so a resumed container would come up without them.
- src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs: `checkDockerContainerExists` — a stopped
  container is exactly the one worth resuming, which the running check hides.
- startKillRecoverySession prefers the in-place path and falls back to the
  previous fresh launch on any refusal; the fallback no longer inherits the
  dead session's execution UUID.

Tests: tests/test-issue-2189-same-container-resume.mjs (31 assertions).
commits.messageHeadline: feat(recovery): resume a killed session in its own container (#2189 R2)

commits.messageBody:
…l` (#2189)

A bot restart orphans the detached-docker completion watchers, so an execution
that ends while the bot is down never gets its exit written — one of the ways
the reported session stayed in limbo. `$ --resume-all` (start-command 0.33.0,
upstream link-foundation/start#164) re-attaches a watcher to what is alive and
finalizes what died meanwhile; it starts no work on its own.

Runs before the durable store is replayed so the first monitor tick reads
settled state. An older `$` without the verb, a refusal, or a thrown error
can never stop the bot from coming up.

…y default

@sentry/node 10.71+ defaults `enableLogs` to `true`, and structured logs are
delivered through `beforeSendLog` — `beforeSend` never sees them. The redaction
this repository relies on was therefore no longer covering everything that left
the process (issue #2189).

`src/instrument.sanitize.lib.mjs` extracts the sanitizer so `beforeSend` and the

commits.messageBody:
…o exit 1

@changesets/cli 3.0 throws `ExitError(1)` from `changeset version` when there
are no unreleased changesets; 2.x warned and exited 0. The release job decides
to release from a changeset count read *before* rebasing onto the remote, and
the rebase can consume the very changesets that decision was made on when a
concurrent run versioned them first — a no-op under 2.x, a red release job for a
healthy repository under 3.x (issue #2189).

`versionAndCommit` re-reads the count after the rebase and reports the version
already on disk through the existing `already_released` contract, so the case
stays the quiet self-healing outcome it was. Reproduced first, in
tests/test-issue-2189-changesets-3-version-guard.mjs.

…ed assertion

Both `$` wrappers fell back to an interpolated exit code, which is `null` for a
child ended by a signal — exactly the "exited with code null" that hid an
out-of-memory kill for a whole session in issue #2135. They now use
`describeChildExit`, so the signal is named when there is one.

`tests/test-issue-1980-docker-cleanup.mjs` asserts on the source text of
`findStartCommandBinary`, which this branch moved into
src/start-command-cli.lib.mjs (the resume wrappers need the `$` loader without
importing the runner and creating a cycle). The assertion follows the function;
the guarantee it pins — the probe must not mirror `which $` to stdout — is
unchanged.

…as malformed

prettier 3.9.6 drops the space before a `for` header's empty third clause and
reflows markdown that earlier versions left alone, so 23 documents and two
sources are reformatted with no change in meaning.

Four of those markdown files were genuinely malformed rather than merely
unformatted: single-tilde ranges rendered as strikethrough, a `|` inside a code
span split a table cell, and a code span containing a backtick was delimited
with one backtick instead of two. Each is repaired so GFM renders what the
author meant (issue #2189).

Two dependency claims are recorded as *not* applying here rather than assumed:

reproductions are in experiments/issue-2189/, along with the jscpd config probe.

The four READMEs document what a killed session now does — resumed in its own
container by default, with `--on-session-kill=report` to opt out — in all four
supported languages.

commits.messageBody:
command-stream normalizes a signalled exit to 128+signum before the caller sees
it, so there is no `null` code to guard against at these two sites and no signal
to pass. The reason to use describeChildExit here is the one issue #2135
established: one vocabulary for how a child ended, everywhere.
commits.messageHeadline: docs(isolation): say why describeChildExit is used, accurately

…efresh logs

The "every spawner reports the signal rather than interpolating a null code"
guard already covered src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs, and it is what caught this
branch's first draft of the `$` wrappers. src/isolation-runner.resume.lib.mjs
is a spawner too and now reports through describeChildExit, so it joins the
list — the module this branch introduced is held to the same rule as the seven
that came before it.

The case-study verification logs are re-run against the branch as it now
stands: 432/432 test files pass (was 425 at v2.15.1), lint and format:check are
clean, and the fail-closed credential scan is regenerated over the new
npm-test.log — still 19 files, 3 with sanitizer rewrites, all of them the
documented keyword-proximity false positives. secretlint over the folder is
empty.
